decision: Continue unchanged joint-memory versus bilateral rows on bank2, in both orders. The matched feedback ablation supports the component while third-bank stability remains untested.
evidence: Feedback gains0.2867/0.3039pp; all single-task deletion averages stay positive in both orders. First two calibrated stages have exact matching coefficients and native weights.
limits: One selected bank, two correlated orders, exposed development validation. Feedback changes both memory directions and their spectrum; this ablation does not separate orientation selection from amplitude effects. No novelty or broad stability claim follows automatically.
further_conditional_question: If bank2 supports development, test whether the benefit persists against an original-direction control scaled to the feedback-induced slot norms. This distinguishes directional retention from amplitude/conditioning; do not launch that experiment during bank2 just to occupy hardware.
